title: EV Charging Hardware: DC, AC and BESS | Anari Energy
meta: DC fast charging from 20 to 960 kW, AC wallboxes from 3.5 to 22 kW and liquid-cooled storage from 120 to 418 kWh — with the selection logic behind each family.

sections.h1: Equipment for every part of the charging network.
sections.lede: Six hardware families: five DC fast-charging families and liquid-cooled battery storage. The right family is decided by the site constraint — headroom, duty cycle, climate or available capacity — not by the power rating alone.
sections.credit: ANARI charger production line, staged before shipment

sections.h2: Start with the constraint, then compare within the family
sections.lede: Ratings overlap deliberately: four families cover 60–240 kW because the decision between them is about expansion, connector standard and enclosure — not about how many kilowatts are printed on the datasheet.

sections.lede: Same site, three candidate answers. Values are the published specifications; the “Choose it when” row is the selection logic, not a sales line.

fora.name: Fora
fora.form: Central power cabinet + up to 16 dispensers
fora.connectors: CCS2 / GB/T · liquid-cooled up to 600 A
fora.best_for: Very high-throughput corridors and hubs where one site must serve many bays
fora.efficiency: Liquid-cooled 0–600 A terminals; OCPP 1.6J native, 2.0.1 compatible
fora.expansion: Add dispensers to the same cabinet (6/8/10/12/16 configurations)

vulco.name: Vulco
vulco.best_for: Sites expected to grow: start on the power you have and add modules when utilisation justifies it
vulco.climate: Reserved heater interface for sub-zero regions
vulco.expansion: 120 → 480 kW upgrade path without replacing the cabinet

pales.name: Pales
pales.connectors: 2 × DC: CCS2 (250 A) and GB/T (250 A)
pales.best_for: Mixed fleets that must accept both CCS2 and GB/T at one station
pales.expansion: Power configurable at order; no field module upgrade

castor.name: Castor
castor.best_for: Small sites, depots and destination parking where a full cabinet is oversized
castor.expansion: Add units per bay; no shared cabinet

aquila.name: Aquila
aquila.connectors: 2 × DC: CCS2 (200 A) and GB/T (250 A)
aquila.best_for: High-footfall commercial sites where advertising or tenant revenue closes part of the business case
aquila.efficiency: OCPP 1.6J · image ads standard, video on request

bess.name: BESS 120 / 261 / 418 kWh
bess.connectors: Pairs with any DC family on site
bess.best_for: Weak grid, peak shaving or off-grid: storage is sized before the charger is chosen
bess.expansion: AC-side parallel to GWh scale (418 kWh) · on/off-grid transfer <50 ms

sections.h2: Storage when the grid is the constraint
sections.lede: Liquid-cooled LFP cabinets from 120 to 418 kWh pair with any DC family to shave peak demand, bridge an unreliable connection or run a site that has no grid at all.
This is the order we actually use on projects. It is the same order the ROI calculator models when it asks for capex and power together.

items.title: Headroom
items.text: If the fleet will grow, a modular DC platform beats a fixed cabinet.

items.title: Connector standard
items.text: CCS2, GB/T or both — dual-standard sites narrow the choice quickly.

items.title: Enclosure & climate
items.text: Ambient heat, dust and monsoon decide the cooling and sealing spec.

items.title: Grid capacity
items.text: If the transformer cannot grow, storage enters the design before the charger does.

items.title: Operating model
items.text: Remote sites need serviceable modules, not sealed single-unit cabinets.

sections.h2: Send the site parameters and we will return a configuration.
sections.lede: Available kVA, dwell pattern, connector standard and climate are enough to narrow the family in one exchange.
